timeline.event: Mumtaz Mahal dies; Shah Jahan commissions the Taj Mahal
Construction begins under architect Ustad Ahmad Lahori
Main mausoleum structure completed
Entire complex completed — gardens, mosque, guest house
UNESCO World Heritage Site designation
Construction begins when Shah Jahan shifts capital to Delhi
Fort completed; becomes the residence of Mughal emperors
Nadir Shah invades and loots the fort including the Peacock Throne
Last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar holds court here during the revolt
UNESCO World Heritage Site designation

name: Qutub Minar
builder: Qutb ud-Din Aibak, continued by Iltutmish

timeline.event: Construction begun by Qutb ud-Din Aibak after defeating the last Hindu kingdom in Delhi
Top three storeys completed by Iltutmish
Top storey damaged by lightning; Firoz Shah Tughlaq repairs and adds two more storeys
UNESCO World Heritage Site designation
Construction begins under Emperor Vespasian
Inaugurated by Emperor Titus with 100 days of games
Major fire caused by lightning damages the upper levels
Powerful earthquake causes the entire south side to collapse
Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site

name: Eiffel Tower
unesco_status: Part of 'Paris, Banks of the Seine' UNESCO site (1991)

timeline.event: Maurice Koechlin and Émile Nouguier create the initial design
Construction begins on the Champ de Mars
Completed for the Exposition Universelle; becomes world's tallest structure at 300m
Antenna added, increasing height to 330m
Included in the UNESCO 'Paris, Banks of the Seine' World Heritage Site
Great Pyramid of Khufu construction begins
Great Pyramid completed — tallest man-made structure for 3,800 years
Pyramid of Khafre and the Great Sphinx constructed
Pyramid of Menkaure, the smallest of the three, completed
Memphis Necropolis designated UNESCO World Heritage Site

name: Machu Picchu
builder: Emperor Pachacuti of the Inca Empire

timeline.event: Built as an estate for Emperor Pachacuti
Abandoned during the Spanish Conquest
Rediscovered by American historian Hiram Bingham III
Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Built by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh so royal women could observe street life without being seen
Jaipur painted pink to welcome Prince of Wales — Hawa Mahal included
Major restoration project completed
Construction begins under King Suryavarman II
Temple complex completed — largest religious monument in the world
Gradually converted from Hindu to Buddhist temple
Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Foundation stone laid to commemorate the visit of King George V and Queen Mary
Construction completed; ceremonial arch opened
Last British troops march through the Gateway, symbolizing the end of British rule in India
Construction begins under Pericles' building program
Colossal chryselephantine statue of Athena by Phidias installed
Sculptural decoration completed
Venetian bombardment causes massive explosion, destroying the roof
Acropolis designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site

name: Statue of Liberty
builder: Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi (sculptor), Alexandre Gustave Eiffel (structural engineer)

timeline.event: Construction begins in France
Statue completed in Paris and disassembled for shipping
Dedicated in New York Harbor — a gift from France
Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site

name: Mahatma Gandhi
builder: Father of the Nation, Freedom Fighter
unesco_status: Recognized by UN International Day of Non-Violence (Oct 2)
significance: Pioneered the philosophy and strategy of nonviolent civil disobedience (Satyagraha) that liberated India from colonial rule and inspired international civil rights and freedom movements worldwide, including those led by Martin Luther King Jr. and Nelson Mandela.

timeline.event: Born in Porbandar, Gujarat, India.
Arrives in South Africa; develops the strategy of Satyagraha (truth-force) over 21 years.
Returns to India and leads nationwide peasant and labor movements in Champaran and Kheda.
Leads the iconic 240-mile Salt March to Dandi, shaking the economic and moral foundations of British rule.
Launches the Quit India Movement demanding an immediate British exit.
India achieves freedom; Gandhi conducts fasts unto death to restore communal harmony.
Martyred in New Delhi; celebrated universally as a global icon of peace and liberty.

name: Swami Vivekananda
builder: Monk, Philosopher, Founder of Ramakrishna Mission
unesco_status: National Youth Day (Jan 12) & Global Interfaith Pioneer
significance: Introduced the ancient Indian philosophical schools of Vedanta and Yoga to the Western world with his historic 1893 address at the Parliament of Religions in Chicago. Revitalized India's cultural confidence and spiritual renaissance, advocating selfless service to humanity.

timeline.event: Born Narendranath Datta in Kolkata, Bengal.
Meets mystic master Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa at Dakshineswar.
Delivers his epochal speech ('Sisters and brothers of America') at the Parliament of Religions in Chicago.
Founds the Ramakrishna Mission for universal human service, relief, and education.
Establishes Belur Math as the monastic headquarters of the Ramakrishna Order.
Attains Mahasamadhi at Belur Math at age 39, leaving an immortal intellectual legacy.

name: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose
builder: Supreme Commander of Azad Hind Fauj (INA)
significance: Led the armed freedom struggle for India's liberation as Supreme Commander of the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj). Coined the immortal national greeting 'Jai Hind' and mobilized thousands across Asia, delivering decisive blows to British imperial confidence.

timeline.event: Born in Cuttack, Orissa Division.
Ranks 4th in the Indian Civil Service exam in London, but resigns to join the national freedom movement.
Elected President of the Indian National Congress at Haripura.
Executes the 'Great Escape' from British house arrest in Kolkata to Europe and Southeast Asia.
Proclaims the Provisional Government of Free India (Arzi Hukumat-e-Azad Hind) and takes command of INA.
INA troops raise the Indian tricolor in Moirang, Manipur on Indian soil.
Reported martyred following a plane crash; revered across the nation as Netaji.

name: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
builder: Chief Architect of Indian Constitution, 1st Law Minister
unesco_status: Conferred Bharat Ratna (1990) & World Human Rights Pioneer
significance: Chief architect of the Constitution of India, world-renowned jurist, and economist who led the historic movement for Dalit rights and the eradication of social untouchability. Enshrined equal rights, civil liberties, and progressive labor laws into the foundation of the world's largest democracy.

timeline.event: Born in Mhow, Central Provinces (Madhya Pradesh).
Earns master's and PhD from Columbia University, New York, and D.Sc from London School of Economics.
Leads the Mahad Satyagraha to claim equal public water access for Dalits.
Concludes the Poona Pact with Mahatma Gandhi for reserved legislative seats.
Appointed independent India's first Law Minister and Chairman of the Constitution Drafting Committee.
The Constitution of India drafted under his leadership takes effect on January 26.
Embraces Buddhism alongside 500,000 followers at Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur.

name: Albert Einstein
unesco_status: 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics & Time Person of the Century
significance: Fundamentally transformed our understanding of space, time, gravity, and energy. Formulated the Special and General Theories of Relativity and the mass-energy equivalence equation E=mc^2. His Nobel Prize-winning work on the photoelectric effect was pivotal to the emergence of quantum physics.

timeline.event: Born in Ulm, Kingdom of Württemberg, Germany.
Annus Mirabilis: publishes 4 revolutionary papers on the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, and special relativity.
Completes the General Theory of Relativity, proving gravity is the geometric warping of spacetime.
Sir Arthur Eddington's solar eclipse expedition experimentally verifies gravitational light bending.
Awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect.
Immigrates to the United States and joins the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton.
Passes away in Princeton, New Jersey, celebrated as the greatest scientist of the modern era.

name: Abraham Lincoln
unesco_status: Signer of Emancipation Proclamation & Lincoln Memorial
significance: Preserved the United States through its greatest existential crisis, the American Civil War, while defeating the Confederacy. Issued the Emancipation Proclamation and secured the Thirteenth Amendment, legally abolishing slavery in the United States and elevating democracy to its highest moral ground.

timeline.event: Born in a humble one-room log cabin in Hardin County, Kentucky.
Elected the 16th President of the United States.
Civil War begins; mobilizes the Union to preserve constitutional government.
Issues the Emancipation Proclamation freeing slaves in rebel states and delivers the Gettysburg Address.
Pushes through the 13th Amendment abolishing slavery; delivers Second Inaugural ('With malice toward none').
Assassinated by John Wilkes Booth at Ford's Theatre just days after the Confederate surrender.
